task:
Yes, <Ranger>, we've got something for you. The main office of our company - Nevits & Gnik - is located on <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. They've been facing serious problems there with their...uh, 'project'. You'll learn all the details on location. I must warn you that your life will be in grave danger if you accept this mission. You will need nerves of steel to cope with everything there. But if you succeed, the fantastic sum of <Money> cr. will be deposited into your account.

Oh, and I almost forgot. You have to arrive on the planet no later than <Date>.
success: Hey, there you are, <Ranger>! Stop flailing about. Calm down. It's not every day that you get a chance to visit a horror amusement park for free! We could even name some monster after you. Maybe, '<Ranger> the Evil Stinking Demon'. That should make you happy! Okay, okay. Stop yelling. Here's your money, <Money> cr.! Do come and visit us again here at Nevits & Gnik!
loc.1.0: You leave the ship, squinting your eyes from the bright light of the star <ToStar>. You look around for the attendants. There’s nobody on the airfield. You go to the spaceport building, but nobody is waiting with a sign for <Ranger>. There are only hundreds of humans, pelengs and faes dashing about. For some reason you don't see any maloqs and gaals. Deep in thought, you perch yourself at a bar counter. A maloq bartender is lazily wiping glasses and watching the stereovision located above the counter. There's a hatchball game on. You order a glass of guanava and sink even deeper into thought. You are in danger of failing to accomplish your mission - you have nowhere to go and nothing to do. But you can't get those <Money> cr. out of your mind.
loc.2.0: You sit at the bar for a while, but nothing happens. You voice your displeasure and stroll sadly toward your ship. The galaxy is waiting for a hero; there's no time to waste here.
loc.3.0: The broadcast of the hatchball game is interrupted by an ad for a new horror film. A plaintive offscreen voice prophesies of a new apocalypse and hordes of bloodthirsty monsters. Meanwhile, you can see a brawny maloq girl splashing <clr>alcohol<clrEnd> from a bottle on a disgusting vampire. The miserable vampire steams and gnashes with its claws, wailing even louder than the girl. Finally, the ad is over and the hatchball game continues. Unfortunately for you, both of the teams playing were quite pathetic. You grow bored of players' vain attempts and turn away from the stereovision, sinking deep into thought.
loc.3.1: You try to watch the hatchball game - it’s rather pitiful. The players wander around the field and the ball moves slowly from one side to the other. Ultimately, you feel asleep from boredom, slumped off your stool, and hit your chin on the floor. Rubbing your injury, you turn away from the screen.
loc.4.0:
You bang your glass on the counter to attract the bartender's attention. Since no one else is in the bar, the bartender leaves his glasses and approaches you. You start chatting about the war against the dominators, a military coup d'etat on planet <ToPlanet>, and the best-ever guanava recipe. Finally, you manage to get the bartender to say something. He treats you to a cocktail and reports the latest news.
"What can I say, <Ranger>? What good can happen on a blasted human planet? Nothing at all! No coup d'etat, no armed conflict, not even a big war... These humans only know how to do business. They are developing a so-called post-industrial society! Some run-of-the-mill companies like Nevits & Gnik keep a low profile. They've been constructing something in this isolated area for more than a year. They won't let anyone enter the site! The confounded officials seem to have come to an agreement with them. They don't poke their noses into their business! I'm telling you, <Ranger>, no good will come of this, or I'm a lying maloq...
Suddenly, you recalled that Nevits & Gnik is the name of the company that has brought you to this planet. If Machpella won't come to the Ranger, the Ranger must go to Machpella.
"Hey, pal. Can you help me out? Where is that...uh...run-of-the-mill company located?
"Sure! Helping a ranger is no trouble for a maloq. It's only seven blocks away. You can get there in no time on the surface train."
Just then a group of tipsy pelengs and humans flocked into the bar. The bartender said, "Well, good luck, pal," and left to wait on the new arrivals. You swallow the rest of your cocktail, hop off the chair, and head for the exit.
loc.5.0:
You tear yourself away from the chair and stroll back to the spaceport to look for your escorts. Along your way, you encounter several humans, faes, and pelengs, who keep bumping into you, apologizing, and then moving on resolutely. Your search fails again, but you do find a food stand. The person at the counter becomes very animated, trying to draw your attention. Why not buy something to eat?

"Come by and buy!" he shouts. "I've got the finest delicacy at a ridiculous price - a marvelous meat sandwich for only {20} cr! Also fresh and tasty white bread for only {18} cr! And if you're thirsty, I've got blasted mineral water - all natural and healthy! I'll sell it to you for half price: only {15} cr!" 

As you approach, he gives you a sidelong look and says that only today - and only to you - he can sell a bottle of the finest rubbing alcohol (96% proof) at a ridiculous price of {50} cr.
loc.5.1:
The bread is packed in a shrink-wrapped plastic bag. The label says that it's made using an ancient human recipe and that it's very wholesome for all races. You pay the salesman and take the bread. However, for a long time you are plagued with the thought that freshly baked bread should be soft, not as hard as your ship's hull. Certainly, the salesman knows best - just look at his engaging smile...

You are at the food stand. You can buy some food as a reserve. You might need it.
loc.5.2:
Your eyes notice a bottle of mineral water "Mineral Quaka". And according to its advertising, it's literally packed with very beneficial and extremely healthy substances. You buy it and unscrew the cap. After taking a sip, your tears start to flow. So what if the water has a greenish hue and stinks of sulfur? The point is that it's healthy.

You are at the food stand. You can buy some food as a reserve. You might need it.
loc.5.3:
You are staring eagerly at a sandwich loaded with a mixture of herbs and exotic spices. The middle of it is crowned with a golden piece of well-done meat. After a brief moment of deliberation, you buy the sandwich and hide it in your pocket unwillingly. Lunch must wait. It may come in handy somewhere.

You are at the food stand. You can buy some food as a reserve. You might need it.
loc.5.4:
What would a trip be without a bottle of alcohol? It's so versatile! You can use it to treat wounds, wipe windows, or make fire! And there must be dozens of other uses!

You are at the food stand. You can buy some food as a reserve. You might need it.
loc.6.0:
Deep in thought, you perch yourself at a bar counter. A maloq bartender is lazily wiping glasses and watching the stereovision located above the counter. There's a hatchball game on. You order a glass of guanava and sink even deeper into thought. 
You are in danger of failing to accomplish your mission - you have nowhere to go and nothing to do. But you can't get those <Money> cr. out of your mind.
loc.8.0:
You reach the nearest surface station and take the express train to Nevits & Gnik's company offices. While the train's silver body races quietly along over the city, you wonder what sort of business the company is involved in.
An old gaal enters the wagon at one of the stops. He sits down in front of you and opens a holographic newspaper. As it is semitransparent, you can see the text. Though it is difficult to read from the opposite side, you manage to read one of the articles:
"FAEYAN TOURISTS’ MYSTERIOUS DISAPPEARANCE STILL UNSOLVED"
"The editor recently received information about the disappearance of a small group of three faeyan tourists. According to the missing persons' ID cards, they are residents of Aipentak and had come to <ToPlanet> to see its ancient architectural sights. The last person to see the faes was an employee of the hotel where the missing faes were staying. By his account, the faes went out for walk around the city at night, but they didn’t return. The planet authorities have launched an official investigation. The Ambassador of Aipentak has arrived on the planet. He is extremely troubled by the incident.
Some witnesses claim to have seen somebody throwing faeyan bodies into the river... More details on page 7"
The gaal glances at the article, but opens to page 9, which describes a revolutionary new method of self-awareness based on astral communication with your ego. Looking away from the newspaper, you realize that you have already arrived at your destination.
loc.10.0:
Unable to stop trembling, you turn around and start walking away - slowly at first, then faster and faster - as far away from this gloomy mansion as you can get. You seem to hear either groans or growls coming from the half-open entrance door, as if some creature had lost its prey... 
You got back to the surface station as quickly as your legs would carry you. You cast all thoughts of <Money> cr. aside and rush from there to the spaceport, swearing to yourself that you'll never again accept any mission without finding out everything about it first.
loc.11.0:
You don’t have to search for long. There's a holographic banner with the company name fluttering near a majestic old mansion. Built after the manner of the humans of ancient times, the structure is quite impressive. Though it is very old and dilapidated. The square windows on its walls, which have turned black with time, seem to watch the passers-by. Together with a part of the roof, they are covered with thick, shriveled ivy. The house looks as if its owner abandoned it long ago. It seems to be dead inside, but it still stands like a silent giant.

Just looking at it makes you shiver and fills you with despair. These thoughts are unbecoming of a ranger. You pull yourself together and drive these thoughts away. You try to think through your assignment. This mansion is totally different from anything you would find in the mission of your dreams. It is too lonely and gloomy... Anyway, the mission is still possible. Perhaps you should go inside? You come back to reality and feel somebody watching you. You could almost swear there was somebody watching you from a window on the second floor. After a while, the illusion vanishes.

You push aside the creaking door of a monumental but rusty gate and head to the front door. Your path lies through an area that has long since been abandoned and overrun with weeds. A huge, tattered raven sits on a stick protruding from the soil. He follows you with his bulging, discolored eyes and caws from time to time. You glance at the sky and discover that dusk is approaching. The star <ToStar>, half-shrouded behind clouds, sinks slowing below the horizon, filling the place with sinister waning light. Finally, you reach the mansion's doors.
loc.11.1:
You grasp the massive bronze door knocker that hangs from a rope and start rapping on the door with it.
Smash!...
Smash!...
Smash!...
Everything around you suddenly seems to begin vibrating. It's as if the house is behind a curtain of hot air - its outlines are drifting and distorted...
Regaining consciousness, you find yourself in the very same place. The mansion, just as before, looms gloomily and gigantic - nothing has changed. You wipe the sweat off your forehead. It was just an illusion. You must have drunk too much guanava.

You stand at the mansion's doors. It's getting dark. <ToStar>, half-shrouded behind clouds, sinks slowly below the horizon, filling the place with a sinister waning light. From time to time, the house creaks on the inside and rustles on the outside.
loc.13.0: You're in a dismal but spacious hall. At a distance, there are two semicircular stairs that lead to the second floor. There are three doors on the first floor. There is a pedestal in the middle of the hall, but there is no statue on it. You draw closer and try to read the inscription on the pedestal, but you can’t decipher the language. Where will you go?
loc.13.1:
You're in a dismal but spacious hall. At a distance, there are two semicircular stairs that lead to the second floor. The stairs on the left have collapsed. A black hole with splinters of rotted wood grins in its place.
There are three doors on the first floor. There is a pedestal in the middle of the hall, but there is no statue on it. You draw closer and try to read the inscription on the pedestal, but you can’t decipher the language. Where will you go?
loc.14.0:
You are in an empty and dreary passage. There are stairs behind you that lead to the first floor. There are five identical doors in the passage. The second door is boarded shut with planks of wood. There doesn't seem to be any way to open it.
Where will you go?
loc.15.0:
You enter and close the door tightly behind you. The furnishings in the third room were scarce. On the far wall of the narrow, rectangular room, there is a huge mirror that rises to the ceiling, set in a wide carved frame. The glass has dimmed with time, but it is entirely free of dust. An armchair rests in front of the mirror. You follow some vague intuition and take a seat in the armchair. You start thinking over your next move. The armchair is modern. Its soft upholstery is heated and warms your back nicely. The sound of a crackling fire emanate from speakers built into the chair. You drift into slumber and dream that you are back at home sitting in front of the fireplace and reading the memoirs of the Ranger who defeated Machpella.

Suddenly, you wake up, as if someone had just barked your name right in your ear. You listen carefully, but can hear nothing other than a soft rustle coming from the speakers. Just then you look in the mirror and see that the door that you had closed tightly is now open. Strange... You whip around and look at the door. Everything is just fine. The door isn't open.

You almost die of fear right there in the armchair. You try to calm yourself by saying that it's only some optical illusion caused by light reflecting through the window. After deciding that it is yet another side effect of the shot of guanava you downed back at the spaceport bar (that seems like such a long time ago!), you notice through the mirror that the door keeps opening. But the door in the room is still closed.

Suddenly, something white and limp falls onto the carpet through the widening crack in the door. Horrified, you recognize what it is: an arm. Judging by its shape, it could have belonged to a human or a faeyan. You jump from the armchair and start retreating away from the door. The arm isn't doing a thing, except clawing the floor with its fingers. You know that the arm isn't really there. What do you do? What if you go toward the door and encounter the owner of the arm?
loc.16.0: You are about to leave the room before the creature returns. You turn back to the mirror and see the door in the mirror swinging wide open. There it is, standing in the doorway. Neither fae nor human. It's difficult to say what it is exactly. One thing is certain: it’s dead. It has a torn cloak made of rough fabric that didn't hide the pieces of flesh on its ribs. The creature's face is touched with decay. Sniffing at your reflection, its mouth wrinkles into some kind of a smile. <clr>The monster has no eyes - just black holes<clrEnd>; But its sharp teeth are in excellent condition. Silently chomping them together, it moves toward your reflection.
loc.17.0:
The beast tosses the gnawed leg aside and approaches the mirror, touching it with its long white fingers. Bloody fingerprints appear on the glass of the mirror. The creature definitely wants to go from the mirror world into yours. It strikes the glass with its fists several times. The glass rattles, but withstands the hits.
The creature picks up the gnawed leg again and starts aiming at the glass. You retreat, reaching for the door handle.
Crash!
A web of fine cracks spreads across the glass. The creature grins mischievously with its rotten maw and hits the mirror one more time. A big piece of glass shatters and a bloodstained hand immediately appears from behind, fumbling in the air. You gasp in horror and try to fling the door open. The rest of the glass crashes to the ground behind you, and you can hear greedy sniffing and screaming behind you...
What will you do?
loc.18.0:
You head to the middle door, stepping cautiously across the creaking floorboards. The door is quite plain, made of rough wood without any decorations. It squeaks when you open it to enter the room.
The room is very small, three meters wide by three meters long. There isn't anything especially remarkable about it, except for one small detail.
A huge semi-transparent bell is suspended in the middle of the room. Its bell's surface, which is either made of glass or silicon plastic, shimmers in the light like a force field. Confused, you stare at the bell. You cannot understand what it is for or how it got here. Its surface seems to produce a faint, almost inaudible, buzzing noise.
What do you do next?
loc.18.1:
Wielding a heavy iron hammer, you approach the bell. Bells are made to be hit, right? Is it here for nothing?
You swing the hammer and strike the bell’s shimmering surface as hard as possible.
The sound from the impact deafens you. A huge tongue seems to have come to life inside the bell; it now lashes out at the semi-transparent sides. The ringing of the glass pierces the mansion.
The sound of the bell eventually stops, but it is replaced by other sounds. The ringing has awakened the mansion - puffing, hungry growls, gnashing claws, and shrill howls can be heard everywhere. Soon all is silent again, but you can't help but think that the inhabitants of the house now know of your presence - and you can’t wander the mansion alone.
Lowering the hammer, you turn away from the bell.
loc.18.2:
You swing your arm and strike the bell’s shimmering surface as hard as possible with your fist. Nothing happens. The bell doesn’t ring and continues to buzz quietly. Only your fist now hurts... Apparently, you'll have to hit the bell <clr>with something more substantial<clrEnd>.

You’re in a small room, looking at a sinister semi-transparent bell. You can hear it buzzing faintly. What do you do next?
loc.18.3: You’re in a small room, looking at a sinister semi-transparent bell. You can hear it buzzing faintly. What do you do next?
loc.19.0:
You take the bottled water from the pocket of your trusty Ranger overalls and approach the bell. Bells are made to be hit, right? Is it here for nothing? You swing the bottle and strike the bell’s shimmering surface as hard as possible.

Nothing happens.

The bell keeps buzzing quietly. The remaining water slides slowly down its surface. Confused, you stare at the bell and the sharp neck of the broken bottle in your hand. You failed to ring the bell, but now you have a weapon... You weigh the sharp glass in your hand. It could be used effectively to slit a throat if there are monsters in the house. But maybe you should throw it away so that it doesn’t cause any problems for you.
loc.19.1:
You remove the bottle of alcohol from the pocket of your trusty Ranger overalls, take a swig for courage, and approach the bell. Bells are made to be hit, right? Is it here for nothing? You swing the bottle and strike the bell’s shimmering surface as hard as possible.

Nothing happens.

The bell keeps buzzing quietly. The remaining alcohol drips slowly to the ground. Confused, you stare at the bell and then at a sharp neck of the broken bottle in your hand. You failed to ring the bell, but now you have a weapon... You weigh the sharp glass in your hand. It could be used effectively to slice a throat if there are monsters in the house. But maybe you should throw it away so that it doesn’t cause any problems for you.
loc.21.0:
You approach the fifth door. It's an automated door that senses your approach; it swings open, loudly striking the wall. You enter the room.

Apparently, it's a study. A blinking plasma lamp hangs from the ceiling. The only thing in the room is a huge desk covered with laptops and plastic printouts. In the middle, is a computer's damaged and non-functioning halo-protector. On the wall there is also a scratched videophone with a receiver and broken screen.
loc.21.1:
You lift the receiver from the videophone and try to call the spaceport to see if your escorts have arrived. The speaker has been ripped out, but you stare, quite annoyed, at the wires hanging from the receiver. You are about to put the receiver back when you suddenly hear a faint whisper. Promptly turning pale, you look around to find the source, your eyes coming to a rest on the videophone.
There can be no mistake about it. Despite the lack of a speaker, the whisper originated from the receiver.
Hesitatingly, you hold the receiver to your ear.
"to her... Let me speak to her... Just speak... I've called...I've called, I remember that for sure... Just speak... There is no one here, not a single person, but I should speak to her... She hasn't come... Why?... Things to do... Nothing to put on... Or is there?.. She'll come... But things to do... She is busy... But that will pass and she'll come, sure..."
You held the receiver to your ear too quickly; the wires touch you and delivered a painful shock. You scream and drop the receiver. It breaks to pieces as it crashes into the floor.
The whispers stop.
loc.21.2: You look at the papers on the table. They are covered with rows of figures and unfamiliar bureaucratic jargon. Trying desperately to find anything valuable on the table, you open its drawers and find a little holographic photo album entitled "Me and Cesska Ritz". An inscription at the bottom reads, "I hate Shitzka!". In the next drawer you see a small <clr>plastic card<clrEnd> marked "/P.K./2/1/". It looks like the card should open some electronic lock. You stash it in your pocket.
loc.21.3:
You take the album from the drawer and activate it. The device starts functioning, though with a bit of interference. An idyllic scene appears in the air before you.  A young peleng female is walking along a bog with her boyfriend.  She is rather attractive - at least for a peleng. The caption under the hologram reads: "Me and Cesska Ritz at the Mossy Bog". She could be seen hanging out with this Cesska Ritz in other photos as well; in some she was feeding phatklinks with him. And she had a good time at the Slime-Bog Festival. But soon other sorts of images began to appear. In particular, the photo of the same young girl at two grave-bubbles in a funeral bog with the laconic caption "Mourning"; and a photo of Cesska Ritz shaking hands with an unfamiliar peleng, with the caption "The best lyakushas I know".
Then you come across photos that look as though they were taken by a hidden camera. One of them depicts an unfamiliar female peleng with a bouquet of slime in her hands. Another peleng stood away from the camera, his face out of view. The caption reads: "Shitzka! Traitress!"
Suddenly, the image dies away. You open the device and discover that the battery level is zero. You return the device to the box and leave the table.
loc.23.0:
You begin to go up the left stairs. After rising only a couple of steps, the stairs begin to creak ominously under your feet. There is a loud crash of rotting wood breaking, and then the whole staircase collapses abruptly. Everything is covered with clouds of dust. You fall onto something soft. Debris falls on top of you. When you finally clear your throat of the dust and wipe your watery eyes, you see a big, jagged gap above you. Looking around, you enter a dark vault with no source of light. It is a tunnel with walls of bare earth.

You hop off the soft mass you had fallen onto and then realize that it was the corpse of a gobsaurus. Its green skin shines dimly in the light passing through the gap. The gobsaurus seemed to be dead, but it must not have been for very long. It's huge corpse had not yet begun to decompose. Shuddering, you slide down from the gobsaurus and run off. You've got to get out!
loc.26.0:
As you approach the first door, a click sounds suddenly from deep inside and a small slot appears in its center. You look at it and even poke your finger in it, but there is no reaction. In trying to open the door, you see that it is locked and has no handle.
How can you open it?
loc.27.0:
You bring the card to the crack and suddenly it gets sucked inside. After a loud click, the door slides silently into the wall. A short passage lies before you, leading to another door. It has no handle, but it does have a speaker and a microphone. You move forward into the passage. Looking back, you see without being very surprised that the outer door has already closed. And there's nothing you can do about it. You approach the door and pick up the microphone. The speaker suddenly comes to life, and a voice is heard. It is a female peleng.
"Who... Who's there? You've come already? Who is that?"

You can hear in the female peleng's voice that she is expecting an answer. You try to remember all that you saw in the drawer in the fifth room. From all appearances, the person behind the door is the owner of that office. Who was to visit her? What should you answer?
loc.27.1:
- <Ranger>?.. No, I don't know you! Go away! I don't want to speak to you. I'm expecting a visitor soon, do you hear? Go away until after he’s gone. Quickly!
The speaker remains silent for some time and then asks again: "Who's there?"
What should you answer now?
loc.27.2:
"That's a LIE!" The voice suddenly becomes very high and you can hear hysterical sobs. "I don't have any parents! I buried them myself! I remember...I remember the smell of that bog and their grave-bubbles!"
Suddenly, the voice shrieks. You cover your ears and recoil in fear away from the speaker. The voice gradually fades away and the sobbing stops. Soon the speaker again asks: "Who's there?"
You return to the speaker, still trembling slightly.
loc.27.3:
Suddenly, the door bulges towards you, as if a furious gobsaurus had rammed into it.
"YOU VILE WENCH!!! You stole my Cesska Ritz! He was mine, you understand, MINE!!! I HATE YOU!!!
You run to the opposite end of the passage, fearful that the creature behind the door might break out and attack you. But the door stands fast. After another absolutely furious blow, there’s silence. The door has straightened right up, leaving no sign of damage.
Trembling fearfully, you return to the speaker.
loc.27.4:
YOU?! The speaker cracks from the female peleng’s fierce shout. You dare come here after what you did?! I've seen it...all of it! You gave that wench a slime bouquet as a gift! You betrayed me! Tell me right now. I don't mean anything to you, DO I?! Do YOU love HER?! ANSWER ME!!!
Wide, jagged holes with appeared in the door right before your very eyes, as if someone had shot at the door with a plasma weapon from the other side. You fall to the floor to take cover from the shots. Everything suddenly ceases and you see that there are no holes in the door. The speaker is silent for a while, but then asks: "Who's there?"
Trying to maintain your composure, you get up off the ground.
loc.29.0: "What?... Is that you?" The voice in the speaker becomes warmer. "Cesska Ritz?"
loc.31.0:
The speaker remains silent. You had decided that the young female peleng didn't want to speak to you when the door suddenly hit the wall, opening a typical bedroom to your view. And there standing before you, wrapped in a towel, is the same young female peleng you'd seen on the photos. As far as pelengs go, she was nice indeed.
"You... You lied to me. You're not that lyakusha."
You gulp nervously.
"That lyakusha is my only support now. After Shitzka, my best friend... You know Shitzka, right?.. She stole my Ritz! And my lyakusha used to be friends with that traitor Ritz... By the way, he promised to come visit! He'll be here soon! Will you help me?..."
The female peleng looks at you expectantly. Suddenly, you notice that the edge of the bed is slightly visible through her body. You'd better not make her angry - you don't know what she's capable of.
"Yes... Of course. What am I to do?"
"The dress. You know, my dress! It was here, but I've lost it... It seems... I don't remember... It must be somewhere nearby. You'll find it, won't you? I can't come before my lyakusha like this... I need only my dress - that's all! If I get it, we'll be together! Go. Find it. Take this, it will help you..."
The female peleng throws a magnetic key to you.
"It will help you... But it's not that easy, one key isn't enough, yeah...
With these words, she turns away wandering aimlessly about the room, looking in the closet and under the bed. She's forgotten all about you. Trying not to disturb her again, you go out to the passage. The door closes behind you with a quiet rumble.
loc.32.chg.0:
Suddenly, the door bulges towards you, as if a furious gobsaurus had rammed into it.
 "YOU VILE WENCH!!! You stole my Cesska Ritz! He was mine, you understand, MINE!!! I HATE YOU!!!"
You run to the opposite end of the passage, afraid that the creature behind the door might break out and attack you. But the door stands fast. Suddenly, you realize that you can't stand another moment in that damned house and you rush away. After encountering a closed door, you begin thrashing it with your fists, sobbing in horror. You soon lose consciousness due to your panic.

After a short time, you realize that you are in the other world. You open your eyes. What seems to be an angel appears. Blinking, you realize that it's no angel - just an ordinary man.
 "What’s happened to me? Am I dead?"
 "Not at all! You're in a mental hospital now. We picked you up near the new building at Nevits & Gnik. Let's just get things out in the open right away. Have you been taking hallucinogenic drugs?
You shake your head and try to organize your thoughts.
 "No... But that cursed house... There are ghosts and spirits everywhere!"
The doctor shakes his head disappointedly.
"You see! You're still being affected by the hallucinogens. We're discharging you now, but if I were you, I’d give up the drugs.
You leave hospital at maximum speed and head for the spaceport, escaping as far as possible from that damned house. Though you failed to find an explanation for what was happening, nothing can make you return to the mansion, not even <Money> cr., which you will not be receiving.
loc.34.0: You approach the right door and pull on it. The door doesn’t give. Examining it carefully, you notice a small groove. It might be a slot for some sort of key.
loc.36.0: Which ring should be removed now?
loc.36.1: Marvelous! You collected all the rings on one pole. I wonder what will happen next.
loc.37.0: You pull a heavy stone ring from the top row. The relief images of skulls dig into your hands. Where can this heavy thing be hung?
loc.38.0: You pull a stone ring off of the middle pole and, struggling to keep it in your hands, you wonder what pole it should go on.
loc.39.0: You pull a ring from the bottom row and placing it edgewise on the floor. You lean on it and look at the other poles. Which one should you hang the ring on?
loc.40.0:
As soon as you step back from the poles to admire your work, they suddenly fall into the wall along with the rings. A small door swings open in the far wall, and a small hollow appears in the wall next to you. Drawing closer to the hollow, you notice with pleasure that it contains an excellent <clr>dagger<clrEnd> with wavy edges and a ridged handle. You take the dagger from the hollow. It seems to be made just for you. It fits in your palm very comfortably. You wave it around. What a perfect weapon! Just what you need! 

You approach the opening and see the corpse of a peleng, but not just any peleng. It belongs to the very female whose spirit had spoken to you in the first room. The body seems to have been there for a long time. It's stained with rot all over, though it doesn’t stink. The worst thing was that the corpse was wearing a green, four-sleeved <clr>dress<clrEnd> in perfect condition. This must be the dress the peleng girl was looking for. How can you get it to her?
loc.40.1:
You begin forcing the small door. It gives way little by little. Unexpectedly, just then the skulls on the rings started talking!

"Look at him!" said the human skulls. He doesn't want to solve the puzzle!
"That is just immoral!" the gaalian skulls answer indignantly.
"He's probably just too stupid," said the faeyan skulls.
"Or he's too cowardly!!!” growled the maloq skulls.
"People like that turn into snitches!” concluded the peleng skulls.

"Shut up!!!" you shout, nearly completely losing your temper. The skulls shut up, the poles fall immediately into the wall together with the rings, and the door swings open by itself.

You see a peleng corpse lying in the opening, but not just any peleng. It's the same girl whose spirit spoke to you in the first room. The body seems to have been there for ages. It's covered with rotting stains, though it doesn't stink. The worst thing was that the corpse was wearing a green, four-sleeved <clr>dress<clrEnd> in perfect condition. This must be the dress the peleng girl was looking for. How can you get it to her?
loc.41.0:
Trying to hold your burden more comfortably, you approach the door. It instantly disappeared into the wall. The peleng girl is standing in the opening, wrapped up in a towel and semi-transparent, just as before. Her eyes shine with excitement.
"Well? Have you found it? Give it to me!"
You reach out to offer her the dress. She grabs it at once and presses it to herself. But she is not pleased. She approaches you and looks in your eyes. It’s like someone is breathing on you with the coldness of a graveyard. You step back.
"You..." hisses the peleng girl. "You took this dress off of me? Are you insane...? YOU'LL PAY FOR THAT!"

You try to raise some objection, but you have no time. The dress is suddenly on the peleng girl, but she's transforming. Narrow greenish claws grow from all sixteen fingers. Her pupils contract into vertical slits, and a hollow roar - quite uncommon among pelengs - is coming from her throat. You move back to the door, unsurprised to find it closed. The creature facing you no longer bares any similarity to a peleng. It moves slowly toward you, intending to pierce you with its greenish claws. There's nothing else to do. You must accept the fight!
loc.41.1: The creature rushes forward promptly, and you have no time to jump aside as it sticks its long fangs into your neck and steps back immediately. Blood from your neck stains your ranger suit, but you feel no pain.
loc.41.2: The creature rushes at you, exposing its claws. You try to evade, but it makes contact. Slanting deep gashes appear across your chest, but for some reason you feel no pain.
loc.41.3: The creature rushes at you in an attempt to pierce you with its claws and thrash you, but you jump aside. The former peleng girl realizes that she missed and turns to you with a furious cry.

Moving the portrait to the side, you notice an object wrapped in fabric. It's an ancient iron key, the kind used for mechanical locks. You slip it immediately into the pocket of your ranger suit and leave the room. The door slams behind you, apparently forever.

"Day three. The healing potion is almost ready. I have enough ingredients to make ten gulps. I was afraid I wouldn't have time to get quanga leaves by midnight, but everything turned out fine. loc.51.0:
You pass through the tunnel, holding to the rough earthen wall. The slightly illuminated opening disappears around a curve of the tunnel, and you find yourself in total darkness. You'll need to make your way by touch. Fortunately, the passage is straight, without any offshoots, so you are in no danger of getting lost.
Finally, after wandering in the darkness for fifteen minutes, you notice some light. As you draw nearer, you realize the light is coming from a lamp standing in a small room. The room has two doors in addition to the passage from which you entered. You were about to pass into the room and choose one of the doors when you got the feeling that there is something moving on the ceiling.
Taking a close look, your voice fails you. There's a giant spider hanging from the ceiling - it’s not much smaller than an average gravicar. You imagine what would happen if the spider attacked you. You gulp.
Something must be done.

Judging by its shape, the hole is part of a mechanical lock. It is designed for a primitive iron key.
loc.52.1: You examine the well-lit room, which has two doors. One of them is made of wood and is very thick. loc.53.1: The spider rushes forward with incredible speed for its size. It seizes your body in its mandible. With incredible effort, you manage to liberate yourself from the spider's vice. There are two deep, fresh wounds on your body, but you feel no pain.
loc.53.2: The spider strikes at you with its sharp-tipped legs, weaving and dodging you impressively. You fall backward. Narrow cuts appear on your body. But still no pain...
loc.53.3: The spider rushes towards you. You decide to apply your military cunning and you fall flat to the ground. Unable to stop, the spider flies right over you. Suddenly, the spider begins emitting disgusting sounds - something between crunching and hissing - and then begins spinning itself around. The alcohol seems to dissolve the spider. Huge pieces of chitin fall off its body and its fur decays right before your very eyes.

loc.54.5: You wave your weapon furiously, trying to attack the spider. You succeed. The spider jumps aside, its body trembling, and bluish blood flowing from fresh wounds.

loc.54.7: You wave your weapon furiously, trying to attack the spider. However, it drops down on all eight legs, practically hugging the floor, and your powerful swing whiffs through the air over its torso.
loc.54.8: You jump back from the monster and munch on the sandwich. You immediately feel more vigorous and some of your wounds heal.

Near the walls you notice five small statues representing something strange. Each seems to symbolize a sense. The nearest statue has no ears. An inscription in front of it reads: "Hearing". There is a statue without a nose with the inscription "Smell", a statue without eyes with the inscription "Sight"; a statue without a mouth with the inscription "Taste", and even a statue representing a creature without skin. Its inscription reads "Touch".

It seems like you have to choose the statue that symbolizes the sense that your enemy lacks.

loc.58.2: The statue jumps at you, pointing its stone claws forward, but you manage to block the blow and force it aside. The statue regrouped in the air and, upon landing, turns towards you again.
loc.58.3: The statue jumps at you, swinging wide with its claws. The stone claws are very sharp and deep cuts appear on your face and chest. Blood floods into your eyes, but you feel no pain at all...

loc.62.0:
You approach the door that is nailed over with boards, casting a disappointed look at it. You ponder how it might be opened easily. Suddenly, the door trembles, as if someone delivered a devastating blow against it from the other side. You raise the hammer and step back from the door.

Another blow... Most of the boards couldn't endure it - they burst and scatter. One more blow... The door breaks from its hinges and crashes against the opposite wall, sending clouds of dust into the air. Plaster falls from the ceiling. 

Ranger <Ranger> stands in the opening.
Unbelieving, you stare at your own face. But your twin is a little bit different than you: his skin is somewhat darker; his eyes look bloodshot; and his ranger suit is tattered and smudged with blood. He is twirling a hammer in his hands though, an exact copy of yours. He probably used that very hammer to knock down the door. 

Still twirling the hammer in hands, your twin prepares for an attack, concentrating his malicious, narrow eyes on you. You must accept the fight and attack the enemy!
loc.62.1: Your opponent swings the hammer to attack you. You try and succeed in dodging the blow. After your incredible evasive maneuver, you let the hammer fly over your head.
loc.62.2: Your opponent swings the hammer furiously to attack you. You try to evade the blow, but it was too broad for you to manage to escape the zone of devastation. The hammer strikes your body and you hear your own bones crunch. But there is no pain.

loc.62.4: The enemy rushes abruptly forward, swinging his hammer. You get hit hard enough to cause instant hemorrhaging. Yet, despite the serious wound, you feel no pain.

loc.63.3: You make a long, slanting swing with the hammer to attack your enemy with less force but more certainty. But your opponent moves backward, and you, still being pulled by the inertia of your undelivered blow, are barely able to straighten up.

loc.66.0:
Once at the gate, you notice that there's company waiting for you. But even if they are the very archdemons of hell, they can't stop you from abandoning this cursed house. You climb the fence quickly and find yourself before a small crowd of happy gaals, faes, humans and pelengs.
Confused, you stare at their joyful faces. You hang on to your hammer just in case. An elderly gaal steps forward. He seems very familiar, like you've seen him somewhere before. Yes, that's right. He was sitting in front of you in the railcar reading the article about the lost faes.
"My dear, Ranger <Ranger>! On behalf of all of us here at Nevits & Gnik, I congratulate you on successfully accomplishing the task before you! You've done a brilliant job testing our new park of horrors. You've demonstrated that everything works as it should! What do you think of those lifelike droids - the giant spider, the spirit of the peleng girl, and your own twin? And how about our holographic system for displaying wounds? There's nothing else like it! You've got to admit that your wounds looked entirely realistic, but you felt no pain at all! I'm not sure if you saw our mirror monster or not.  He's our pride and joy. Where else can you find such a marvelous holographic mirror projection?...
The gaal stopped short as you swung at him with your hammer. He quickly shielded himself from you with a huge check which read "<Money> cr." in big, fat letters.
"Hey, now! Hey!... I confess, we went a bit too far. We didn't warn you about the task, and we failed to meet you... But that was all intended to make the testing as realistic as possible! I sat in front of you in the railcar with that bogus article about the faes in order to intensify the effect. We didn’t know you would be so squeamish!
Your rage disappeared quickly, being subdued by the cheque and your honor as a ranger.
"I haven't been afraid at all. You've got a good park here. Maybe I'll call on you. Later. After the war is over, no sooner."
The joyful procession brings you to the spaceport, and you, waving to them with one hand and stroking the check in your pocket with the other, vow to yourself that you will never undertake another mission without fully understanding its requirements.
loc.67.0: Suddenly, you notice a flat, steel disk, about the size of the palm of a hand, lying on the floor by the bar counter. Upon closer examination, the disk turns out to be an anniversary-edition maloq coin for {50} cr. with the profile of the prince Tardim Babach. You almost put the coin into your pocket, but it was too inconvenient to carry another 5 kilos. So you exchange the coin for bills at the bar.
loc.68.0:
You insert the magnetic key into the slot - it fits. The magnetic locks disengage and the door finally gives way. After removing the key from of the slot, you enter a dismal room.

As you enter, torches arranged around the walls flare up on their own. They light up the entire room. There is a small door in the far wall. And right in front of you there are three long poles sticking horizontally out of the left wall. The upper one holds five rings of different diameters, apparently made out of marble. You come closer to look them over. The rim of each ring is decorated with a pattern of skulls. The largest ring is adorned with maloq skulls with well-developed chins and huge superciliary arches, and next smaller ring has peleng skulls with a long horn on top. The middle rings depict human skulls, while the next smaller ones are decorated with faeyan skulls. The very smallest rings are finished with intricate gaalian skulls.

The whole construction arouses vague memories. It's a puzzle as old as the world, created independently by the gaals and the humans in days when neither race had knowledge of space flight. If your memory serves you well, you have to move all the rings from the upper pole to the lower pole, but smaller rings always have to be put on top of larger ones.

You could try to solve the puzzle. You could also try to break down the door by force.

jump.24.desc:
You shrug your shoulders and press the door. You assumed that it would swing open slowly with a creak, but it unexpectedly opens easily and quickly. Underestimating your force, you fall forward, face first, right onto an old, dusty carpet. The door slams shut.
In a panic, you jump up and pull the door towards yourself. Then you push, but it won't open at all. It’s as if it has become a part of the monolithic wall. You sigh sadly and turn away from the door. You look at the furniture in the mansion.
jump.25.text: Go up the stairs on your right.
jump.25.desc: You begin to ascend to the second floor on the stairs to your right. The stairs creak ominously under your feet, but they hold fast. After reaching the second floor, you go into a long empty passage, illuminated by primitive wax-based lighting that hangs from the walls. There are five different doors in the passage. A half-length portrait that covers the whole wall hangs at the end of the passage. But the portrait doesn't depict any person - just a silhouette. You can barely make out the fact that the wording under the portrait matches what was on the pedestal on the first floor.
jump.27.desc:
You rush toward the door, hoping that the creature exists only in the mirror world. Crashing into it with your body, you jump out into the passage and slam shut the door to the room with the mirror. In a panic, you look around and notice an old cyber-mop near the door with a broken intelligence unit. You use it to block the door. Then you step back to the wall and catch your breath. Now if the creature somehow gets out into the real world, it won't be from this room!
With trembling hands you tear your ranger badge from your suit and stare at its shiny surface. Everything is okay. Your reflection is still you.
jump.28.text: Try to use the meat sandwich to entice the creature behind the door.
jump.28.desc:
You take the meat sandwich from your pocket, put it on the floor, and kick it toward the door. The sandwich slides along the surface of the floor and stops right in front of the dreadful hand. The hand instantly grabs it and disappears behind the door. You failed to entice the creature...
Turning around, you make sure that the real sandwich is safe and sound. But it has no reflection any more. You don't dare to pick up the sandwich, being too afraid that the creature might be able to seize your reflection.
jump.29.desc:
You decide to see what's on the other end of the hand, so you approach the door and swing your leg so that your reflection kicks the hand. The hand rushes forward, grabs the reflection of your leg and drags it away behind the door. You stand there with your leg raised, numb with horror. Not trusting your own eyes, you approach the mirror and touch it with your hand.
You have no reflection.
Just then, the mirror door swings open again and the hand is back in front of you - along with its owner. It is neither fae nor human. In fact, it can't really be attributed to any race at all. The one thing that is clear is - it’s dead. It is wearing a cape of tattered, coarse fabric. Beneath the cape, you can clearly see ribs with pieces of flesh. The creature's face is decaying. After sniffing at your reflection, it grins its wrinkled mouth. <clr>The monster has no eyes - just black holes<clrEnd>. Its sharp yellow teeth were gnawing on something that you recognize with a shudder as your own leg.
Then the creature stares at you from the mirror. It seems to feel you...
jump.30.desc:
In an attempt to save both your reflection and yourself, you jump to the side to slip past the creature. You rush toward the door, jump out into the passage, and slam the door shut behind you. In a panic, you look around and notice an old cyber-mop near the door with a broken intelligence unit. You use it to block the door. Then you step back to the wall and catch your breath. You could hear more blows and the sound of the shattering glass behind the door. The monster seems to have entered the real world!
The creature claws at the door for a while, but then falls silent. With trembling hands you tear your ranger badge from your suit and stare at its shiny surface.  Everything is okay. Your reflection is still with you.
jump.32.desc:
You tear a massive leg from an armchair that is unexpectedly fragile and swing it around, trying to hit the creature's head. Your task is complicated by the fact that you have to constantly look in the mirror. The creature easily evades your swings. While you try to coordinate your actions, it jumps onto your reflection and seizes it by the throat. You're not able to move as you watch weak reflection being dragged behind the door. It is followed by a trail of blood.
You approach the mirror and touch it. You have no reflection any more.
The mirror door suddenly swings open again and the creature returns to the room. It looks stronger and rather satisfied. Its sharp yellow teeth are gnawing on something that you recognize with a shudder as your own leg.
It looks around and stares right into your eyes. It seems to feel you...
jump.33.desc:
You swing the door wide, jump out into the passage and slam the door shut right on the creature's nose. You hear a deafening crash, a shriek, and the gnashing of claws on wood. In a panic, you look around and notice an old cyber-mop near the door with a broken intelligence unit. You use it to block the door. Then you step back to the wall and catch your breath.
The creature claws at the door for a while, but then falls silent. Trying to catch your breath, you curse the employees of Nevits & Gnik with the most offensive words. You've lost your reflection because of their horrifying task!
jump.37.text: Hit the bell with the bottle of alcohol.
jump.38.text: Hit the bell with the bottle of water.
jump.40.text: Get rid of the sharp glass.
jump.41.text: Hit the bell with your fist.
jump.44.desc: You approach a thick metal door which looks quite odd among the mansion's ancient furniture. You pull its handle forcefully. The door moves slightly and you can hear a primitive mechanical lock give a resonant crack. You don't notice a keyhole. It doesn't appear that the door can be opened from that side.
jump.54.text: Insert the card into the slot.
jump.58.text: It's Shitzka. So you remember me?
jump.59.text: I'm the best lyakusha you know!
jump.69.text: Insert the magnetic key into the slot.

jump.72.text: Hang it on the third row.
jump.72.desc: You roll the ring to the bottom pole near the floor and hang it there.
jump.73.text: Take the ring from the second row.
jump.74.text: Hang it on the first row.
jump.74.desc: Straining all your muscles, you lift the ring to the very top and hang it on the upper pole.
jump.75.text: Hang it on the third row.
jump.75.desc: You roll the ring to the bottom pole near the floor and hang it there.
jump.76.text: Remove the ring from the third row.
jump.77.text: Hang it on the first row.
jump.77.desc: Straining all your muscles, you lift the ring to the very top and hang it on the upper pole.
jump.78.text: Hang it on the second row.
jump.78.desc: Holding the ring at chest level, you bring it to the middle pole and hang it cautiously. Now you should rearrange the other rings.
jump.79.desc: You give up on the difficult puzzle and start to leave the room. An obscure grinding sound came from behind you, and when you turn around, all the rings have been moved to the upper pole.
jump.80.text: Wait for the effect to kick in.
jump.84.desc: Deciding not to dishonor the poor peleng girl, you lift her body from the floor and, holding her in your arms, bring her out of the room. The peleng girl turns out to be unexpectedly light - it's easy to get to the main hall. The magnetic door slams behind you. Only now do you discover that you lost the magnetic key back in the pole room. The way there seems forbidden to you from now on...
jump.85.desc: Damning yourself and screwing up your face from time to time, you begin taking off the dead peleng girl's dress. You feel like a total pervert. Nevertheless, soon the dress is in your hands. Trying to avoid looking at the naked peleng girl's corpse lying on the floor, you come out into the main hall. The magnetic door slams behind you. Suddenly, you discover that you lost the magnetic key back in the pole room. The way there seems forbidden to you from now on...
jump.87.desc:
Trying to hold your burden more comfortably, you approach the door. It disappears into the wall immediately. The peleng girl is standing in the opening, wrapped up in a towel and semi-transparent, just as before. Her eyes shine with excitement.
 "Well? Have you found it? Give it to me!"
You bend down and lay her body in front of her. It is strange to see the peleng girl standing over her own body. However, she expresses no surprise when looking at her body. She just strokes her dress, looks at it happily, and mutters something. Little by little, she becomes even more transparent, until she fades away completely. You seem to have saved her soul. Just imagine! A couple of hours ago you would have laughed at the idea of a ghost really existing, but now you've helped one of them...
However, you have things to do. As the peleng girl fades away, it becomes possible to examine her room fearlessly.
jump.88.text: Hit the creature with your fists.
jump.90.text: Strike with your weapon at an angle.
jump.92.text: Strike with your weapon at an angle.
jump.97.desc:
When you manage to hit the creature again, it suddenly falls down on the floor and lies still. A pool of blood slowly accumulates underneath it. Surprised, you notice that all your wounds have disappeared, as if they had never existed. But you don't have time to be surprised. 
Stepping over the defeated monster, you enter the peleng girl's room to examine it properly.
jump.99.desc: The fourth door has an ancient maloq style. It isn't finished, but it is made of very hard wood and reinforced with wide iron strips. Pushing the door open, you enter a room that reminds you of a library. It's quite strange to find a library behind a maloq door, but you begin to examine it just the same.
jump.104.text: Read the book lying near the pot.
jump.110.text: Throw a sandwich in the pot.
jump.113.desc: You switch the plasma heater on and the contents of the pot disappear immediately behind a silver clouds of vapor. In seconds the vapor is gone. The pot is filled with a silver liquid. You open the empty water bottle and begin to fill it with the liquid. The contents of the pot just fit into the bottle, which holds about ten gulps. Well, now you have a healing potion!
jump.114.desc: You switch the plasma heater on, and everything disappears immediately behind a puff of smoke. Coughing and sneezing, you manage to turn the heater off. The contents of the pot burn down, leaving behind a disgusting-smelling, sticky mess. You failed to prepare the potion...
jump.115.text: Swallow a little bit of the potion.
jump.120.text: Distract the spider by throwing it the sandwich.
jump.120.desc: You swing good and hard and throw the sandwich into the room. The spider waits for some time. Then, deciding that the sandwich is not a living creature, it gets down and clicks its mandible over it, rolls it up in a web, and creeps away, dragging its prey into a hole in the ceiling. Perfect! The spider is gone. Now you can examine both doors in peace.
jump.121.text: Distract the spider by throwing it the bread.
jump.121.desc: You swing good and hard and throw the bread into the room. The spider notices that the bread is not a living creature, it gets down and grasps its mandible over it, rolls it up in a web, and creeps away, dragging its prey into a hole in the ceiling. Perfect! The spider is gone. Now you can examine both doors in peace.
jump.123.text: Hit the spider with your fists.
jump.125.text: Strike with your weapon at an angle.
jump.127.text: Strike with your weapon at an angle.
jump.132.text: Swallow a little bit of the potion.
jump.133.desc:
The spider suddenly tumbles over sideways, throwing its legs upward. You strike it cautiously, but it is indeed dead. Suddenly you notice that all your wounds have disappeared, leaving no scars.
Stepping over the spider's body, you examine the two-door room.
jump.136.desc: You remove the bolt from the door and discover that it goes right into the main hall of the mansion. It was the door on the left that you couldn't open from the hall.
jump.138.text: Open the door with the iron key.
jump.138.desc:
You insert the key into the hole and turn it. A metal click sounds and the door swings open. You remove the key and stash it in your pocket. Then you enter the room and look around. It is one of the gloomiest rooms you’ve seen in the mansion. The walls are made of rough stone, and the floor is covered with coarse granite slabs. A pedestal towers at the end of the room. Something can be seen resting on it under a glass dome. Drawing closer, you see that it is a heavy hammer with a long handle. It seems to be made of iron. Its surface is covered with freakish runes that you've never seen before. You don't even try to get the hammer out from under the glass dome. Instead, you look around and notice some writing on the wall behind the hammer.

"Bravery test.
Our familiar world borders a different world. It reflects the exact opposite of our reality. This results in creatures like the one you must encounter. This creature is capable of killing your reflection - and you. But if you want the reward, then you must meet it face to face... Just ask yourself: What does your enemy lack?"

The writing is in the universally-known intergalactic language and, if you aren't mistaken, the style of speech is quite modern. Interesting...What kind of world it is? And what sort of creatures inhabit it?
jump.139.desc: You touch the blind statue and wait for the reaction. At first, it seems that nothing will happen, but then the glass dome over the hammer opens with a click. You take <clr>the hammer<clrEnd>. The handle feels pleasantly cool in your hands. Its reliable weight reassures you. You approach the door. Then all the statues suddenly jump down from their pedestals and rush in your direction. You jump behind the door in and instant and slam it shut. You insert the key into the keyhole, turn it, and, just to be sure, break it. They claw at the door from the other side, but can’t break it open. Now no one can enter or exit the room.
jump.140.desc: As soon as you touch the deaf statue it jumps from its pedestal and rushes toward you. It seems to be extremely hostile... You must have failed to solve the puzzle.
jump.141.text: Choose the statue symbolizing the sense of smell.
jump.141.desc: As soon as you touch the statue without a nose, it jumps from its pedestal and rushes toward you. It seems to be extremely hostile... You must have failed to solve the puzzle.
jump.142.desc: As soon as you touch, with disgust, the loathsome statue without any skin, it jumps from its pedestal and rushes toward you. It seems to be extremely hostile... You must have failed to solve the puzzle.
jump.143.desc: As soon as you touch the statue without a mouth, it jumps from its pedestal and rushes toward you. It seems to be extremely hostile... You must have failed to solve the puzzle.
jump.145.text: Hit the bell with the hammer.
jump.146.text: Hit the statue with your fists.
jump.147.text: Strike with your weapon at an angle.
jump.149.text: Strike with your weapon at an angle.
jump.155.text: Swallow a little bit of the potion.
jump.156.desc:
The statue couldn't withstand another blow. Suddenly, it cracks in two and sinks to the floor, covered by clouds of stone hash. When the fight ends, you notice with surprise that all your wounds have disappeared.
As you turn away from the pedestal where the statue had been standing, you notice that a secret door has opened in the pedestal and a similar statue has appeared from there. It isn't moving - it's just standing peacefully. You decide not to touch it any more...
jump.162.text: Strike from above with the hammer.
jump.163.text: Strike from above with the hammer.
jump.164.text: Strike from the side with the hammer.
jump.165.text: Strike from the side with the hammer.
jump.166.text: Swallow a little bit of the potion.
jump.173.desc:
Your twin couldn't withstand your latest attack. He just falls to the ground like a sack of sand. It is very unpleasant and unusual for you to look at your own corpse, but the passion of victory overcomes your caution - you kick your corpse and begin to examine the room.
There is something in the room that you have been dreaming to see from the very moment the mansion door slammed behind you.
Afraid to believe it, you look at a wide-open window that leads right to the mansion’s rusty gate.
You approach the window and look down. Incredibly, dense ivy bushes have grown by the window. In a minute you climb down along the ivy bushes, and in ten minutes you are at the base of the house. Without looking back, you run toward the gate.
jump.180.text: Forget about the <Money> cr. and fly away.
jump.182.desc: You give up on the difficult puzzle and start to leave the room.
jump.183.text: Wander over to the spaceport to look for your escorts.
jump.184.text: Wander over to the spaceport to look for your escorts.
jump.185.text: Wander over the spaceport anyway and look for your escorts.
jump.188.text: Give up on the puzzle and force the door open.
jump.193.text: Go up the stairs on your right.
param.1.crit:
You realize that you can't stand that damned house any longer and rush away. You run up to locked door and start banging on it with your fists, sobbing in horror. Then, being overwhelmed by panic, you lose consciousness.

Soon you realize that you are beyond the veil. You open your eyes and see an angel leaning over you. After batting your eyes for a while, you realize that it's no angel - just an ordinary man.
"What’s happened to me? Am I dead?"
"Not at all! You’re in a mental hospital. We picked you up near the new building at Nevits & Gnik. Have you been taking hallucinogenic drugs?"
You shake your head and try to organize your thoughts.
"No... That damned house... There are ghosts and spirits everywhere!"
The doctor shook his head sadly.
"There, you see? The hallucinogens are still affecting you. We're going to release you, but you should really stop it with the drugs once you get home."
You leave hospital at maximum speed and head for the spaceport, escaping as far as possible from that damned house. Though you failed to figure out what happened there, nothing - not even <Money> cr. - would lure you back to the mansion.

param.9.crit:
You look at your body in horror - it’s a bloody mess. You lose your concentration and start probing yourself to understand why you feel no pain after your enemy’s vicious attack, which went right through your chest. You discovered the hole in your body before losing consciousness.
Soon you realize that you are beyond the veil. You open your eyes and see an angel leaning over you. After batting your eyes for a while, you realize that it's no angel - just an ordinary man.
 "What’s happened to me? Am I dead?"
 "Not at all! You’re in a mental hospital. We picked you up near the new building at Nevits & Gnik. Have you been taking hallucinogenic drugs?"
You shake your head and try to organize your thoughts.
 "No... But that monster bit right through me!"
You touch your chest, but there is no sign of a wound. In fact, there isn't a single scratch on your body. The doctor shakes his head sadly.
"There, you see? The hallucinogens are still affecting you. We're going to release you, but you should really stop it with the drugs once you get home."
You leave hospital at maximum speed and head for the spaceport, escaping as far as possible from that damned house. Though you failed to figure out what happened there, nothing - not even <Money> cr. - would lure you back to the mansion.
